definition: As Low As Reasonably Practicable. A legal and ethical standard requiring risk to be reduced until the cost of further reduction is grossly disproportionate to the benefit gained. Fundamental to UK/Gulf risk management.

The level of respiratory protection a respirator class provides when used by a trained worker in a properly functioning respirator. N95 APF = 10; half-face APR APF = 10; full-face APR APF = 50; SCBA APF = 10,000.

A sudden release of energy from an electrical arc. Produces extreme heat (up to 35,000°F), blinding light, pressure blast, and molten metal projectiles. Requires arc-rated PPE and energised electrical work permits.

ATmosphères EXplosibles. EU directive governing equipment used in potentially explosive atmospheres. Defines hazardous area zones (0/1/2 for gas; 20/21/22 for dust) and requires Ex-certified equipment in those zones.
An ACGIH reference value for assessing biological monitoring results (e.g., blood or urine samples). Measures the chemical or its metabolites in the body regardless of route of exposure.

Boiling Liquid Expanding Vapour Explosion. Occurs when a pressurised vessel containing a superheated liquid fails catastrophically. The liquid instantly vaporises and, if flammable, ignites. Extremely destructive.

A risk analysis tool that maps the pathway from hazard sources through a top event (loss of control/release) to consequences. Prevention barriers are on the left; mitigation barriers on the right. Widely used in Gulf oil and gas process safety.

UK regulations assigning H&S duties across construction projects to clients, designers, principal designers, principal contractors, and contractors. Requires pre-construction planning and a health and safety file.
The US government's codification of federal regulations. OSHA standards are in Title 29. Part 1910 covers General Industry; Part 1926 covers Construction.
A space large enough to enter, with limited means of entry/exit, not designed for continuous occupancy. Examples: tanks, vessels, silos, sewers, tunnels.

Control of Substances Hazardous to Health. UK regulations requiring employers to prevent or adequately control workers' exposure to hazardous substances. Involves a risk assessment, control hierarchy, health surveillance, and monitoring.

A crane lift requiring a detailed written plan due to complexity, load exceeding 75% of rated capacity, use of multiple cranes, or personnel being lifted. Requires review by a qualified lifting engineer.
Days Away, Restricted duty, or Transfer rate. An OSHA injury/illness rate calculated per 200,000 hours worked. Only includes cases resulting in lost time, restricted duty, or job transfer.
Danger, Response, Airway, Breathing, Circulation. The primary survey sequence used in first aid to assess and manage a casualty. Used globally including in Gulf first aid programmes.
A systematic framework for managing an organisation's environmental responsibilities. ISO 14001 is the international standard for EMS.
Automatic system that safely shuts down process equipment during an emergency. Critical in Gulf oil and gas operations to prevent hydrocarbon releases from escalating.
Fatalities per million hours worked. The standard Gulf and international oil and gas industry KPI for measuring fatal incident frequency. Reported in IOGP annual statistics.

The minimum temperature at which a liquid produces enough vapour to ignite momentarily when exposed to a spark or flame. Flammable liquids (flash point below 100°F/37.8°C) are more hazardous than combustible liquids.

Section 5(a)(1) of the US OSH Act requiring employers to provide employment free from recognised hazards likely to cause death or serious harm. Used when no specific OSHA standard addresses a known hazard.
A safety device that detects current imbalances as small as 5 milliamps and trips in 1/40th of a second. Required on all 120V construction site receptacles under OSHA 1926.404.

International system for classifying and labelling chemicals developed by the UN. Standardises hazard pictograms, signal words (Danger/Warning), hazard statements, and Safety Data Sheet format. Adopted by all Gulf countries.

A highly toxic, flammable, colourless gas with a 'rotten egg' smell at low concentrations. IDLH = 100 ppm. Found in crude oil, natural gas, and sour well production. A life-safety priority across all Gulf operations.

A structured, systematic technique for identifying process hazards using guide words (MORE, LESS, NO, REVERSE, OTHER THAN) applied to design intent. Required for all major process plant in the Gulf. Output: HAZOP register with action items.

Priority order for risk reduction: (1) Eliminate, (2) Substitute, (3) Engineering controls, (4) Administrative controls, (5) PPE. Higher-level controls are more reliable because they do not depend on human behaviour.
Common framework for all ISO management system standards (ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001). Identical clause numbering (1–10) enables integrated management system implementation.

The UK HSE publication 'Managing for Health and Safety' using the Plan-Do-Check-Act framework. Formerly the primary OHSMS guidance in the UK; superseded in practice by ISO 45001 but still referenced in NEBOSH IGC.

term: IDLH (Immediately Dangerous to Life or Health)
definition: The maximum concentration of a hazardous substance from which an unprotected worker could escape without irreversible health effects or impairing escape in 30 minutes. H2S IDLH = 100 ppm; CO IDLH = 1,200 ppm.
See TRIR. A normalised measure of injuries per 200,000 hours worked (equivalent to 100 full-time workers for one year).

International standard for Environmental Management Systems. Requires identification of environmental aspects and impacts, legal compliance, objectives, and continual improvement. Uses the PDCA cycle.

International standard for Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems, replacing OHSAS 18001 in 2018. Emphasises top management leadership, worker participation, risk-based thinking, and continual improvement.

Also called Job Safety Analysis (JSA). A technique that studies the relationship between the worker, the task, the tools, and the work environment to identify hazards and implement controls before work begins.

A programme to detect and repair fugitive emissions from valves, flanges, pumps, and other equipment. Critical for meeting environmental permit requirements and reducing methane/VOC emissions at Gulf refineries and LNG plants.

The minimum concentration of a flammable gas or vapour in air that will ignite. Below the LEL, the mixture is too lean. OSHA requires evacuating above 10% LEL. CH4 LEL = 5%; H2 LEL = 4%; H2S LEL = 4.3%.

A set of non-negotiable safety rules where violation is grounds for immediate dismissal. Aramco, ADNOC, QatarEnergy, and IOGP all use LSRs covering fall protection, driving, LOTO, confined space entry, and work authorisation.

Control of Hazardous Energy. OSHA 1910.147. The practice of isolating all energy sources on equipment before maintenance using personal locks and tags. Prevents unexpected start-up. Called Isolation Certificate on Gulf sites.

Lifting Operations and Lifting Equipment Regulations (UK). Requires all lifting equipment to be strong/stable, marked with SWL, inspected at intervals, and used in a planned/supervised manner. Referenced in Gulf NEBOSH contexts.

A formal process requiring safety review before implementing changes to process, equipment, staffing, or procedures. A PSM requirement (OSHA 1910.119). Critical to preventing incidents at Gulf process facilities.

PSM element requiring documented inspection, testing, and maintenance of critical process equipment including pressure vessels, piping, relief devices, and instrumentation. Prevents catastrophic failure due to corrosion, fatigue, or defects.

Any self-propelled aerial work platform including scissor lifts, boom lifts, and cherry pickers. Used for working at height where scaffolding is impractical. Requires operator training and pre-use inspection.

A laboratory-measured noise attenuation value printed on hearing protector packaging. Real-world protection is approximately NRR/2. Earplugs rated NRR 33 provide roughly 16.5 dB real-world protection.

The maximum airborne concentration of a substance a worker may be exposed to without adverse health effects over a reference period (typically 8-hour TWA). Called PEL in the US, WEL in the UK, TLV by ACGIH.
Former British standard for OHSMS. Replaced by ISO 45001 in 2018. Transition period ended March 2021. Many Gulf facilities still reference OHSAS 18001 in legacy documents.

Abu Dhabi Occupational Safety and Health System Framework. The statutory OHSMS framework for Abu Dhabi Emirate. Includes Codes of Practice (CoPs) covering physical, chemical, biological, and psychosocial hazards.
The minimum score required to pass a NEBOSH examination or quiz. NEBOSH IGC pass mark = 45% per unit with no more than one unit below 30%. NEBOSH Diploma = 50% per unit.
Plan-Do-Check-Act. The continual improvement model underlying ISO 45001 and ISO 14001. Plan: set objectives and processes. Do: implement. Check: monitor performance. Act: correct and improve.

OSHA's legally enforceable maximum concentration of an airborne substance (8-hour TWA unless specified). Found in 29 CFR 1910.1000 Z-tables. Many PELs are outdated; ACGIH TLVs are generally more protective.
A system to arrest a worker who has fallen. Consists of a full-body harness, lanyard or SRL, and an anchor rated at minimum 5,000 lbs. Must stop a fall before the worker contacts a lower level.
A structured analysis of potential hazards in a process system. Methods include HAZOP, What-If, FMEA, and Fault Tree Analysis. Required under OSHA PSM (1910.119) and Gulf operator HSEMS.
OSHA 1910.119. A systematic approach with 14 elements to prevent catastrophic releases of highly hazardous chemicals. Applies when threshold quantities of specified chemicals are present on site.

A formal documented safety management system authorising specific high-risk work. Includes hazard identification, control measures, and sign-off by responsible parties. Mandatory on all major Gulf oil and gas facilities.

Full probabilistic risk analysis producing numerical estimates of individual and societal risk (F-N curves). Used for safety case development at major hazard sites. Expressed as fatalities per year for a defined population.
The combination of the likelihood (probability) of a hazardous event occurring and the severity of the harm it could cause. Risk = Likelihood × Consequence. Assessed on a risk matrix.

A grid-based tool plotting likelihood against consequence to assess and rank risks. Common scales are 5×5 (likelihood 1–5, consequence 1–5). Output: low/medium/high/extreme risk levels requiring different control actions.
A respirator with its own compressed air supply. Required for IDLH atmospheres, oxygen-deficient spaces, and firefighting. APF = 10,000 (supplied-air respirator). Duration typically 30–60 minutes.

A standardised 16-section document providing chemical hazard and safety information. Required under OSHA HazCom and GHS. Formerly called MSDS. Key sections: 2 (Hazards), 4 (First Aid), 8 (PPE/OEL), 9 (Physical Properties).
Saudi Aramco's proprietary OHSMS, equivalent to ISO 45001. Sets minimum HSE standards for all Aramco operations and contractors. Includes General Instructions (GIs) for specific high-risk activities.

The management of two or more hazardous operations occurring at the same time in the same or adjacent areas. A SIMOPS study identifies interface hazards and controls. Critical on Gulf offshore platforms and large EPC projects.

A type of fall arrest device that automatically retracts the lanyard as the worker moves and locks within milliseconds of a fall, limiting fall distance to a few feet. Preferred over shock-absorbing lanyards for dynamic work.

The maximum average airborne concentration of a substance over any 15-minute period that should not be exceeded. A supplement to the TWA OEL for substances that can cause acute effects at short high exposures.

James Reason's accident causation model. Safety barriers are represented as cheese slices — each with holes (latent and active failures). An accident occurs only when holes in all slices align simultaneously.
Task, Individual, Load, Environment. A manual handling risk assessment mnemonic used in NEBOSH IGC and IOSH courses. Assesses four factors before any manual lift.

OSHA metric: (Number of recordable cases × 200,000) / Hours worked. Includes all recordable injuries and illnesses. Used to benchmark safety performance against industry averages. Called TRCFR in Gulf terminology.
The average airborne concentration of a substance over an 8-hour work shift, taking into account variations in concentration and duration. The standard reference period for OEL comparison.

An explosion that occurs when a large unconfined vapour cloud ignites. Generates significant blast overpressure capable of causing major structural damage and mass casualties. Associated with large hydrocarbon releases (Piper Alpha, Texas City).
The UK term for OEL — maximum airborne concentration permitted over an 8-hour TWA or 15-minute STEL. Set by the UK Health and Safety Executive in EH40.

The maximum load that should ever be applied to rigging hardware (slings, shackles, hooks) in normal service. Also called Safe Working Load (SWL). The break load divided by the safety factor (typically 4:1–6:1).
